data.one_liner: Standards-compliant FTP and FTPS server implementation in Dart.
data.what_it_does: Provides a fully-featured FTP and FTPS server running directly inside Dart with support for plain or encrypted TLS, active/passive modes, authentication, and pluggable virtual or physical file system backends.
use_when: You need to embed an FTP or FTPS server into a Dart or Flutter application.
You want to share local files and directories with other devices over the network.
You require standards-compliant RFC file operations without external native server binaries.
avoid_when: You only need an FTP client to connect to external servers.
Your environment does not allow running socket servers.
strengths: Supports plain FTP, explicit FTPS, and implicit FTPS.
Includes zero-config self-signed certificate generation inside Dart.
Pluggable file system backends for virtual multiple directories or a single physical directory.
weaknesses: Dart's SecureSocket limitation prevents sending a TLS close_notify, causing some FTP clients (like FileZilla) to report non-properly terminated directory listings.
Does not support CCC (Clear Command Channel) or REIN under TLS due to Dart SDK socket constraints.
data.setup_notes: No external OpenSSL setup required if using the built-in self-signed certificate generator.
